summary: Chüan-ying Yen works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history and archaeology. She earned her PhD at Harvard University, studying under doctoral supervisor John M. Rosenfield (attested 1986), tutor Chu-tsing Li, and teacher John Hay.

Chün-fang Yü is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. She studied at Columbia University (~1965–1972) and under Nanting and Sheng Yen, later teaching at Rutgers University (~1972–2001) and Columbia University (~2001–2018; Emerita ~2018).

Claes Wennerberg was an Indologist and linguist. He studied under Gösta Liebert and earned his Ph.D. at the University of Gothenburg in 1981, where he later served as a Docent and half-time Universitetslektor.

Claire Chang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and psychology. She earned degrees from the University of Sydney, Naropa University, and Nan Tien Institute, and worked at One Door Mental Health, UC Boulder, and Naropa University (2015–2019).

Clara Sue Kidwell was a historian who earned her master's and Ph.D. at the University of Oklahoma. She held positions at UC Berkeley (~1980–1993), the National Museum of the American Indian, the University of Oklahoma, and UNC Chapel Hill (~2007–2011).

Clare Carlisle is a scholar in philosophy and religious studies. She studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (1995–2002) and held positions at the University of Liverpool (~2006–2011) and King's College London (~2011).

Clarence Herbert Hamilton was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed his A.B. and Ph.D. at the University of Chicago and studied at Union Theological Seminary. He held professorships at Hartford Seminary (1928–1931) and Oberlin College (1931–1952).

Clarence Linton Meader was a linguist and Indologist who earned his A.B. at the University of Michigan and pursued further studies in Athens, Bonn, Munich, and Rome. He served as an instructor in Latin at the University of Michigan (1893–1938).

Claude Charles Fauriel was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Alexander Hamilton and Antoine-Léonard Chézy. He founded the Société Asiatique and was appointed Professor of Foreign Literature at the Sorbonne in 1830.

Claude Hagège is a linguist who studied at the École Normale Supérieure, ENLOV, and Paris Descartes University under André Martinet. His academic career included posts at the University of Poitiers, the EPHE (~1970–1988), and the Collège de France (1988–2006).

Claude Jacques was an Indologist and historian who studied under Armand Minard and George Cœdès. He served as a teacher at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1970–1997) and as director of the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1989–1992).

Claude Lévi-Strauss was a scholar in anthropology and philosophy who studied under Marcel Mauss. He held posts at the University of São Paulo, the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and the Collège de France, where he held the chair of Social Anthropology (1959–1982).

Claude-Auguste Court was active in Indology and archaeology. Educated at the École Polytechnique and École Spéciale Militaire de Saint-Cyr, he served as an engineer officer in the Sikh Khalsa Army and the Court of Ranjit Singh (~1827–1843).

Claudia Benthien is a scholar in linguistics and literature. She earned her MA at Washington University in St. Louis and her Dr. phil and Habilitation at Humboldt University of Berlin, later holding a full professorship at the University of Hamburg (2005).

Claudia Dellacasa works in Buddhist studies. She studied at Sapienza University of Rome and Durham University (PhD 2021) and held fellowships at Tübingen, Augsburg, and University College Dublin before becoming a lecturer at the University of Glasgow in 2024.
Claudia Weber is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who studied under Hans-Joachim Klimkeit and project supervisor Gregor Ahn.

Claudie Marcel-Dubois was an Indologist and ethnomusicologist. She studied at the EPHE under Marcel Mauss and Paul Masson-Oursel and worked at the Musée National des Arts et Traditions Populaires (1937–1981) and the EPHE (1961).
Claudio Giacomino was an Indologist and linguist who served as an ordinary professor of Latin and Greek literature at Liceo Classico Massimo d'Azeglio and held a post at Liceo Chiabrera-Martini.

Claudius Buchanan was a religious studies scholar and Indologist educated at the University of Glasgow and the University of Cambridge. He served as a missionary with the Church Mission Society (1797–1808) and as Vice-Provost at Fort William College (1799).
Claus Haebler was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Friedrich Weller (~1950–1956) and Paul Thieme (~1951–1953). He held a post at the University of Münster (~1972–1996).
